hints: Differentiate x=t²−ln(2t+1) and y=t/(2t+1) separately with respect to t.
Factor the denominator fully and simplify to a single fraction with numerator 1.
walkthrough:
Differentiate $x = t^2 - \ln(2t + 1)$ with respect to $t$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = 2t - \dfrac{2}{2t + 1}$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{2t(2t + 1) - 2}{2t + 1} = \dfrac{4t^2 + 2t - 2}{2t + 1} = \dfrac{2(2t^2 + t - 1)}{2t + 1}$$

Factor the numerator quadratic $2t^2 + t - 1$:
$$2t^2 + t - 1 = (2t - 1)(t + 1)$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{2(2t - 1)(t + 1)}{2t + 1}$$

Differentiate $y = \dfrac{t}{2t + 1}$ with respect to $t$ using the quotient rule:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{(1)(2t + 1) - t(2)}{(2t + 1)^2} = \dfrac{2t + 1 - 2t}{(2t + 1)^2} = \dfrac{1}{(2t + 1)^2}$$

Cancel the common factor $(2t + 1)$ between numerator and denominator:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{1}{2(2t + 1)(2t - 1)(t + 1)}$$
